questions.enonce_markdown:
Jesus gave a new commandment to HIS disciples during the Last Supper. Discuss.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** In the Fourth Gospel the Last Supper (John 13-17) is the setting of Jesus' farewell to his disciples. After washing their feet, he gives them a new commandment: "Just as I have loved you, you also should love one another. By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another" (John 13:34-35).

**1. The setting.** The commandment follows the washing of the disciples' feet (13:1-20), an act of humble service by the master, and the departure of Judas to betray him (13:30). Jesus speaks of his coming departure, saying "where I am going, you cannot come" (13:33). The commandment is therefore Jesus' testament to the community that is to remain after he has gone. In John, unlike the Synoptics, the meal does not include the account of the institution of the bread and cup; the emphasis falls on service and love.

**2. In what sense is it "new"?** The commandment to love one's neighbour was already in the law (Leviticus 19:18). The newness lies in the following:
- *The standard:* "as I have loved you". The model is Jesus himself, whose love goes as far as giving his life (15:13, "no one has greater love than this"), not simply love of self.
- *The motive and source:* the love of the disciples flows from the love of the Father for the Son and of the Son for his own (15:9-10).
- *The community:* it is love "for one another", the shape of a new community of believers, the family of Jesus' friends.
- *The new age:* it belongs to the time of the new covenant, begun by Jesus' death and resurrection.

**3. The content of the commandment.** Love means humble service (the footwashing), faithfulness, readiness to sacrifice, forgiveness and unity. Jesus repeats the commandment in 15:12 and 15:17, and connects it with keeping his commandments (14:15, 15:10).

**4. Its purpose.** It is the visible mark of discipleship: "by this everyone will know" (13:35). The love in the community is a witness to the world. In 17:21-23 Jesus prays for the unity of believers so that the world may believe.

**5. Significance and application.** The first letter of John returns again and again to the same commandment (1 John 3:11, 4:7-12). It is the heart of Christian ethics in John's tradition: the believer loves because God first loved. In practice, it calls Christians to serve across social differences, to be reconciled and to care for the needy.

**Conclusion.** The new commandment given at the Last Supper is that disciples love one another as Jesus has loved them. It is new because of its pattern, Jesus' own sacrificial love, and it is the sign by which the community of believers is recognised.
